title: Economics recommendation response (backend-authoritative)
description: The backend-authoritative recommendation returned by POST /api/v1/economics/recommendation. It leads with the conservative lower bound and ALWAYS carries the spend-$0 case, so a recommendation can never present only an optimistic path. Every dollar figure is a labelled STARTING ASSUMPTION, never a validated one (funnel telemetry is what validates the model), and the contract makes that structural: the formula/assumption identity binds `assumptions_are_starting_assumptions: true`, the budget binds a conservative-lower-bound basis, and the renderable `why` has no member that could claim an assumption was validated. The `why` and the payback explanation are STRUCTURED, closed-vocabulary render tokens the coding agent turns into prose in the user's own terms (their agent, their volume band, their error-cost band) — not an unbounded free-form payload the backend writes for them. The recommendation is independent of credits, pricing, sales incentives, wallet/billing state, and the WI-D funding decision: no such field is representable (additionalProperties:false at every boundary) and none is declared.

contract.description: Names the recommendation contract family, matching the request. A response that does not name it is not a recommendation.

contract_version.description: Stable version of the recommendation contract.

request_id.description: Echo of the submission's request_id, so a recommendation joins back to the characterization it answers.

dominant_value_channel.description: The dominant value channel the recommendation is built around, drawn from the closed characterization vocabulary. Reused by $ref, not restated.

secondary_value_channel.description: An optional secondary value channel. Same closed vocabulary.

why.description: The mandatory explanation, as STRUCTURED render tokens rather than prose: each component names a closed reason and carries typed, bounded operands the coding agent renders in the user's own terms. Required and non-empty because the explanation duty is a product requirement, not decoration — a recommendation with no `why` is incomplete. No component can claim an assumption was validated; the honest counterpart `assumptions_are_starting_not_validated` is the only member that speaks to validation status.

x-backend-obligations: STATUS/FLAG AGREEMENT: a 200 carries this recommendation body. A recommendation the backend cannot compute (insufficient shared characterization) is a 422, not a 200 carrying a fabricated recommendation; a transient inability to compute is a 503. The backend selects the status for the outcome it actually produced.

BUDGET ORDERING: floor_usd <= recommended_daily_usd <= cap_usd must hold. JSON Schema bounds the three amounts independently but cannot relate them; an out-of-order budget is a backend defect to reject at the boundary, not a contract-valid recommendation.

LOWER-BOUND LEADS: recommended_daily_usd is derived from the CONSERVATIVE lower bound of realized value (budget.basis.value_lower_bound), not a point estimate. The contract binds uses_conservative_lower_bound:true and requires the interval, but that the recommended amount actually follows from the lower bound (and not from the point estimate or upper bound) is a computation the backend must honour.

NO PRICING/CREDIT/WALLET INPUT: the recommendation must not be a function of pricing, credits, sales incentives, or wallet/billing state. No such field is representable here or in the request; the backend must likewise not join that state into the computation. Budget floors/caps are labelled starting assumptions, NOT funded amounts — funding is the WI-D owner-gated decision and is out of scope for this contract.

PAYBACK ONLY ON A POSITIVE LOWER BOUND: payback_days is present only when payback.is_lower_bound_positive is true; when the conservative bound is not positive the recommendation leads with the spend-$0 case and claims no payback. The contract enforces the presence rule; that the boolean reflects the real sign of the lower bound is a backend obligation.

ASSUMPTIONS ARE NOT VALIDATED: every dollar figure is a starting assumption. The backend must not present any figure as validated in any rendered or logged form; the funnel/receipt telemetry (WI-B) is what validates the model over time.

PUBLISHED REFERENCE MUST RESOLVE: formula_identity.published_reference is required by the contract, but the schema can only check that a label is present and opaque. The backend must emit a reference that actually resolves to the published, versioned formula + assumptions document for that formula_version and assumption_set_version. Emitting a placeholder, a dangling id, or a reference to an unpublished internal document satisfies the schema and violates this obligation — it would turn the auditability claim into a false one.

formula_version.description: Version of the value/budget formula that produced this recommendation. An opaque label: it names the formula, it does not carry it. Reproducibility rests on the REQUIRED published_reference below plus the design commitment to publish and version that document — the contract can pin the identifiers, it cannot itself prove a document is reachable.

assumption_set_version.description: Version of the assumption set (loaded rates, archetype budgets, default volumes/values) in force. Bumped when a starting assumption changes.

assumptions_are_starting_assumptions.description: Structural honesty label: every dollar figure in this recommendation is a STARTING assumption, not a validated fact. A required const rather than an optional boolean, so a recommendation cannot silently drop the label or set it false to imply its numbers are validated.

published_reference.description: REQUIRED opaque reference to the published formula + assumptions document. Required rather than optional because the credibility claim is that a recommendation is auditable: a response that named only two internal version labels would leave a consumer with nothing to look up, so the claim would outrun the contract. That the reference actually RESOLVES to a published document is a backend obligation the schema cannot enforce (see PUBLISHED REFERENCE MUST RESOLVE). Carries no content.

FormulaIdentity.description: The versioned identity of the formula and assumption set behind this recommendation, plus the structural starting-assumption label. The credibility contract: publish and version the formula and assumptions.

recommended_daily_usd.description: Recommended daily build-phase spend. Derived from the conservative lower bound of realized value (see basis), clamped to the archetype floor/cap. floor_usd <= this <= cap_usd is a backend obligation.

floor_usd.description: The archetype floor for the daily budget. A labelled STARTING ASSUMPTION (see floor_cap_are_starting_assumptions): a floor is not a funded amount, and funding is the WI-D owner-gated decision, out of scope here.

cap_usd.description: The archetype cap for the daily budget. A labelled starting assumption. Narrative cannot raise it: the cap is backend-authored.

floor_cap_are_starting_assumptions.description: Structural label: the floor and cap are starting assumptions, NOT funded balances or credits. A required const so the budget cannot present its floor/cap as anything other than an assumption. Funding (a seven-day credit envelope) is the separate WI-D owner-gated decision; no credit/funding field exists in this contract.

method.description: CLOSED budget-derivation method. 'clamp_floor_cap_fraction_of_conservative_realized_value' is the normal case (a fraction of the lower-bound realized value, clamped to the archetype floor/cap). 'archetype_floor_only' is used when value cannot be estimated but the archetype floor still applies. 'spend_zero_no_positive_lower_bound' records that the conservative bound is not positive, so the recommended amount is the floor and the recommendation leads with the spend-$0 case.

uses_conservative_lower_bound.description: Structural label: the budget is based on the CONSERVATIVE lower bound of realized value, never a point estimate. A required const, so a recommendation cannot quietly base a budget on an optimistic point estimate.

value_lower_bound.description: The estimated realized-value interval the budget is based on, WITH its level, so the lower bound the budget leads with is explicit and a point estimate can never be mistaken for it. May legitimately have a non-positive lower bound (which drives the spend-$0 case). Reused from the common ConfidenceInterval, not restated.

basis.description: How the budget was derived: the closed method, the structural conservative-lower-bound label, and the value interval it leads with.

BuildBudget.description: The recommended daily build budget with its archetype floor and cap and its conservative lower-bound basis. Floors/caps are starting assumptions; nothing here is a funded amount or a credit.

is_lower_bound_positive.description: Whether the conservative lower bound of daily realized value is positive. Payback is only claimed when this is true (see the conditional below): the model must never claim payback from a point estimate when the conservative bound is not positive.

payback_days.description: Conservative payback horizon in days = total optimization cost / conservative daily realized value. Present ONLY when is_lower_bound_positive is true, and FORBIDDEN otherwise (enforced below): a payback number computed from a non-positive bound is exactly the false-positive the credibility rules forbid. Bounded so no unbounded or non-finite value enters the statement.

conservative_daily_realized_value_usd.description: The conservative (lower-bound) daily realized value the payback rests on. SIGNED: it may legitimately be zero or negative, which is precisely the case that forbids a payback claim and leads with spend-$0.

explanation.description: The payback statement's renderable explanation, as STRUCTURED render tokens rather than an unbounded free-form payload: e.g. an avoided_bad_promotion_payback component the agent renders as 'one avoided bad promotion worth $C pays for N weeks of optimization', in the user's own numbers. Bounded and closed.

PaybackStatement.description: The payback statement as structured values plus a bounded renderable explanation. Payback_days exists only on a positive conservative lower bound; otherwise the recommendation carries no payback number and leads with the spend-$0 case.

rule.description: CLOSED stop/continue rule from the economics design. Continue while the value of information plus the incremental lower bound exceeds the next experiment's cost; stop when even the upper bound cannot cover the next cost, or when attainable uptake makes realized value non-positive.

next_experiment_cost_usd.description: The estimated cost of the next experiment the rule is evaluated against. Optional: the rule is stated even before a concrete next experiment is priced.

StopRule.description: The stop/continue rule the client should apply: a closed directive plus the optional next-experiment cost it is evaluated against.

receipt_kind.description: Which machine-verifiable receipt the client must produce before this spend counts as value: winner | defect | savings. Reuses the receipt contract's closed kind enum by $ref rather than restating it, so the recommendation and the receipt it requires cannot drift.

RequiredReceipt.description: The receipt requirement: the kind of independently-verified receipt the client must produce for the recommended spend to count. The receipt itself is submitted through the WI-B receipt contract; this only names which kind is required.

available.description: The spend-$0 case is ALWAYS available. A required const true, so no recommendation can omit or disable it: the user can always choose to spend nothing, and the model leads with the no-spend case whenever the conservative bound is not positive.

explanation.description: The renderable statement of the spend-$0 option, as structured tokens the agent renders in context (e.g. spend_zero_always_available). Bounded and closed.

SpendZeroCase.description: The first-class spend-$0 case, REQUIRED on every recommendation. Making it a required object with `available: const true` means a recommendation cannot be issued that hides the option to spend nothing.

component.description: CLOSED reason token. The coding agent renders it into prose in the user's own terms; the vocabulary is closed so the explanation cannot become a free-text egress channel and cannot make an unbounded set of claims. There is deliberately NO 'assumptions_validated' member — the only validation-status token is 'assumptions_are_starting_not_validated', so a recommendation cannot claim, in structured form, that its dollar assumptions have been validated.

references_field.description: The user's own characterization field this factor is expressed in terms of (e.g. daily_volume_band, error_cost_band), so the agent renders the explanation using the user's actual volumes and error costs rather than generic copy. Drawn from the closed allowlist.

usd_value.description: An optional signed dollar operand for the token (e.g. the avoided-bad-promotion value, a labor-saving estimate). Signed and bounded; it is a starting assumption like every dollar figure here.

number_value.description: An optional numeric operand (e.g. weeks of optimization a receipt pays for, a volume). Bounded.

emphasis.description: Which statistic this factor emphasises. Present so the credibility rule 'lead with the lower bound' is expressible in the render tokens: a value factor emphasising a point or upper bound is visibly not the conservative one.

WhyComponent.description: One structured, renderable explanation factor. Closed reason token plus typed, bounded operands and an optional reference to the user's own characterization field — enough for the coding agent to render the 'why' in the user's terms, and never a free-form prose payload.

x-traigent-note: Contract-first per the workspace cross-repo rule: this response schema lands before the backend recommendation service exists and is NOT asserted against backend parity. The authoritative computation lives in the backend; SDK preflight, portal, and skills are intended to CALL this contract rather than reimplement it. The shipped vectors under tests/test_data/economics/ are schema-valid EXAMPLES of these shapes — nothing implements this contract yet, so they are not conformance evidence for any producer, and no claim is made here that a backend or an offline path agrees with them. Conformance testing starts when the first producer exists. Presentation phrasing lives in the agent's open presentation layer: the backend returns structured render tokens, and the agent turns them into the user's language.
